chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Fadhal, from Abu Jameela, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Night of Pre-Determination (Laylat al-Qadr) is the beginning of the year, and it is the end of it.

key_terms.السَّنَةِ: The year, referring to the Islamic lunar year.
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Pre-Determination, a significant night in Islam, often identified with the 23rd of Ramadan.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Laylat al-Qadr being the beginning and end of the year?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies Laylat al-Qadr as both the beginning and end of the year, a view supported by scholars who interpret this as referring to the lunar year or the year of decree. This dual status underscores the night's pivotal role in divine governance, marking the commencement and conclusion of the annual allocation of sustenance and affairs. The narration highlights the metaphysical significance of this night beyond its temporal placement in Ramadan.
